details_settled_before_the_look.status: Settled by the assistant, outcome-independently, before any Phase 4 code exists and before any block-5 outcome has been read, real or otherwise. Not protocol amendments: where the protocol speaks, the detail follows it. Each is open to the owner's review; changing any now would be a new protocol version stated to follow results of the earlier phases (the development results already exist). Further details that arise during the build are added in a further record committed before the tripwire.

new_in_phase_4.detail: Scope of the look. It evaluates, together and once, every pre-registered predictor on each of the five primary targets in both versions (all_event and clean_window), trained on blocks 1 to 4 as the version sees them: six predictors for a binary target (C1, C2, C3, C4, M2_logistic, M2_without_sector) and five for the regression target (C1, C2, C3, M3_ridge_linear, M3_without_sector), the sensitivities and the cell baselines included. No predictor, target or version is selected or left out. The descriptive report covers all 19 targets in both versions.

COUNTS_ONLY. A target-version whose holdout test events (block 5, with the target defined in that version) have fewer than 10 positives or fewer than 10 negatives (the regression target: fewer than 20 events) is COUNTS_ONLY, as the protocol says: no predictor is fitted or scored for it and no prediction is made, and the report gives the counts, the base rate and its Wilson 95% interval. Every predictor still gets an experiment-log record for it, with the state COUNTS_ONLY and no predictions, so that every cell of the pre-registered grid is accounted for. A target-version whose holdout fold fails the fold-level rule on its training events is INSUFFICIENT_DATA in the same way.

Evaluable target-versions. The metrics are the development ones, computed on the holdout fold alone: precision at K for K = 5 and 10 (the fold values; K = 20 needs 40 events and the fold has 23), reliability in min(4, floor(n / 10)) equal-frequency bins, the contrast of every predictor against C1 and of the pairs the harness lists, by the cluster bootstrap with the protocol's seeds and 5000 replicates, reported at the 95% reporting level (the wider of the reaction-session and issuer intervals, as in the development folds). The same function also computes the 99% level; it is not a holdout statement. Every holdout result carries the protocol's selection-regime statement, and none is a claim.

The sign check. For the confirmatory model against C1 (M2_logistic, or M3_ridge_linear for the regression target) the report states, per version, whether the sign of the holdout estimate equals the sign of the development estimate of the same version (the pooled development out-of-fold contrast in reports/m4-phase2-results-2026-10-07.json or reports/m4-phase3-results-2026-10-07.json). An estimate of exactly zero has no sign. Where the development result is INSUFFICIENT_DATA there is nothing to compare, and the report says so. The check is a statement about direction, not a status.

One look, in order. Before any block-5 outcome is read the runner checks the tripwires, a clean committed tree, the protocol and input hashes, that both logs are exactly as Phase 3 left them (the experiment log with 175 records, the holdout log with its genesis only) and that no Phase 4 output exists. It then calls Harness.look once; the access record is written before anything is unsealed. Everything after that is a pure function of the unsealed events: the evaluation is made twice and the two must be identical, with no second access. No Phase 4 code calls unseal itself.

Technical failure. If the run fails after the look, the access stays on the record. The runner refuses to start unless the holdout log holds only its genesis, so a rerun needs a code change in a commit of its own whose message says it is a technical rerun; the fix must not depend on any holdout result; the rerun is a further logged access and is counted in the report (the protocol's a_technical_rerun). There is no automatic retry.

Dress rehearsal. Before the tripwire is turned on, the whole pipeline (the look, the evaluation, the descriptive report, the report assembly, the logging) is exercised on the real inputs with the real block-5 record files absent and the block-5 labels replaced by seeded synthetic ones, in two regimes (one in which every target meets the holdout thresholds, one in which most do not), against temporary logs and a temporary output directory. It is a test that runs on every CI and reads no block-5 outcome.

Pre-look audit. A structure audit of the holdout fold, taken before the look and reading no outcome: for each primary target and version, the training cells and which fall back to the pooled value, the earlier matured history available to each of the 23 test events (and to the regression target's issuer-history mean), constant indicator features, and the counts of the test events by release timing and sector group, over all 23 test events whether or not the target is defined for them (that depends on outcomes). A test changes every label value and gets the identical audit.

Descriptive report. For all 19 targets in both versions: defined events, positives, negatives, the base rate with its Wilson 95% interval, the protocol's bucket, positives by release timing, issuers and reaction sessions, and defined events and positives by block (1 to 5); for the five regression labels n, mean, standard deviation, standard error and the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles; and the block table by source. It is computed from the 105 visible events and the 23 events unsealed in the one look. It states what the protocol states: block 5's counts of positives were visible in the scoping evidence before the freeze, so the holdout is sealed against model selection and tuning, not against its base rates.

Holdout records. One experiment-log record per predictor, target and version on the fold holdout_test_block_5: 58 records (four binary targets x six predictors x two versions, and the regression target x five predictors x two versions), each with the state EVALUATED, COUNTS_ONLY, INSUFFICIENT_DATA or MODEL_FIT_FAILED, appended after the evaluation has passed its determinism check; the experiment log goes from 175 to 233 records and the holdout log from 1 to 2. Predictions are written for the evaluated cells only, as protocol prediction records timed at the cutoff (B clock) or the regular open (C0 clock).

The tripwire. ALLOW_HOLDOUT_LOOK is turned on in a commit of its own after the build is committed, pushed and green, and turned off again in a commit of its own after the look. Tests pin the holdout log at its genesis plus exactly one access and the tripwire off. Verification after the look replays the look through Harness.look against temporary logs; it never touches the real access log, and no test or script reads a block-5 outcome any other way.

No selection. The look is a replication check on direction and one logged exposure of the frozen pipeline. Whatever the holdout shows, nothing is selected, tuned, re-run with other settings or amended; every predictor is reported; a result that disagrees with the development result is reported as it is. The holdout alone never creates a claim, and no status is assigned from it.

The report. The Milestone 4 report (docs/M4-REPORT.md, and reports/m4-report-2026-10-07.json assembled by code from the committed artifacts) states what was estimable and what was not, every interval with its counts, the number of holdout accesses, the protocol's limits and disclosures, the review items still open for the owner, and, criterion by criterion, the evidence for the protocol's acceptance_of_the_m4_report. It does not declare Milestone 4 accepted: that decision is the owner's.

Open review items. The owner's reply did not address the review items the assistant listed in its closing message (the protocol-silent details in docs/M4-HARNESS.md section 5, the 99% claim level, the thin primaries, the counts-only holdout; the protocol's disclosures.to_review). They stay as they are: the defaults in force, protocol version 1 unchanged, and the report lists them as open for the owner.
